page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-1000s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. This instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-optimized allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 1000 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates strong compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier, while the multi-core CPU performance is strong, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 64051.5. Memory performance is notable, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top tier and uncached read bandwidth measuring 346.3 GB/sec. The system also excels in specialized workloads, showing top-tier performance in LLM text generation for both small and medium models, alongside strong results in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations, which reached 76.91 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of a high memory-to-core ratio. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a deliberate tradeoff, prioritizing raw processing power and local NVMe storage speed over massive memory capacity. This configuration is highly suitable for multi-threaded compilation, ray tracing, text generation inference, and high-throughput caching layers like Redis. It is less optimal for memory-bound database operations or workloads requiring GPU acceleration.
